question.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t)= \left\langle -4, \, \cos{(2t)},\, \sin{(2t)} \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨-4,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16+1} \\  & =\sqrt{17}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+64{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{17}}{\sqrt{17}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
